task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?

turns.thought:

turns.thought:
Yes — all three of those can contribute to exactly the "no data or very slow" symptom you're describing. Here's what I'd suggest, in order:

**1. 2G network connection (most impactful)**
You're connected to 2G, which is far too slow for usable mobile data. Please change your phone's **preferred network mode** to **4G/5G preferred** (in your phone's network/cellular settings — look for "Preferred network mode" or "Network mode"). This lets your phone connect to 4G or 5G instead of falling back to 2G.

**2. Data Saver is ON**
Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make data feel slow or unresponsive. Please turn **Data Saver OFF** in your data usage settings.

**3. VPN is connected**
A VPN can sometimes slow your connection significantly. Could you check what performance level the VPN is reporting? If it shows a **Poor** performance level, please **disconnect the VPN** — that's a common cause of slow speeds.

After changing the network mode and turning off Data Saver, I'd also suggest a **full reboot of your device** so all the changes take effect properly.

Could you make those changes and then check whether your signal shows 4G/5G and whether data is working? Let me know what you see, and if it's still slow, I'll keep digging into it with you.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps for me — I can only do one at a time, so let me take them one by one. I'll start with the network mode since you said that's the biggest factor. Give me a second...

turns.thought: Take your time — no rush at all. Go ahead and change the preferred network mode to **4G/5G preferred**, and let me know once that's done (and what your status bar shows afterward). We'll leave Data Saver and the VPN until you're ready for the next step.

That's a great result — excellent signal on 5G with data enabled. The network mode was the main culprit.

**Next step: turn off Data Saver.**

In your phone's settings, go to the Data Usage / Network section and switch **Data Saver OFF**. This will stop it from restricting background data and limiting your speeds.

Let me know once that's done, and then we'll take a look at the VPN as the last step.

Yes, let's look at the VPN last, as planned.

Please check what **performance level** your VPN is reporting (it usually shows this in the VPN app or in the VPN section of your settings).

- If it shows **Poor** performance — please **disconnect the VPN**, since that's a known cause of slow data speeds.
- If it shows **Good** or another healthy level — you can leave it connected, as it isn't the cause of your problem.

Let me know what it reports, and whether your data feels fast now that you're on 5G with Data Saver off.

Yes, absolutely — a speed test is a great way to confirm everything's working now.

Please run a **speed test** on your phone (using a speed test app or website) and let me know the result — particularly the **download speed** category it reports (very poor, poor, fair, good, or excellent).

Since you need fast internet, if it comes back as anything below **Excellent**, let me know and I'll keep troubleshooting with you.

You're very welcome — glad we got it sorted out! Your summary is exactly right:

**On my side:**
1. Added **2 GB** of data to line 555-123-2002 ($4.00, on your next bill)
2. Enabled **international roaming** at no cost (for your trip to France)

**On your side:**
1. Switched network mode to **4G/5G preferred**
2. Turned **Data Saver OFF**
3. **Disconnected the VPN**
4. Turned on **Data Roaming** on the device

And you're now getting 275 Mbps on 5G — Excellent. 

One quick reminder for later: your 2 GB top-up lasts until your cycle ends on **2025-02-28**, at which point your allowance resets to the standard 15 GB. If you're still abroad after that date and hit your limit again, just reach out and we can sort out another top-up.

Enjoy your time in France, and feel free to contact us anytime if anything else comes up!
